layout: Purchasing → [document] → Define Screen Layout at Document Level. Inspect transaction, activity, document type and item-category field-selection keys.
Material Group can be filled from the material master and still be mandatory under PT0F.
Compare every contributing key before attributing a grey or mandatory field to the Z type.
material: Display the material with MM03 in the relevant organizational views. Review document item category and field selection separately.
A material identifier supplies descriptions, unit and material-group proposals.
Enter the item specification and account assignment required by the client’s item design.
org: SPRO → Enterprise Structure → Definition / Assignment. Review plant, company code and purchasing-organization assignments. Purchasing groups are maintained under MM → Purchasing.
The order is delivered to one specified plant.
One organization may buy for multiple plants; check assignments and saved item values.
inventory: Inspect plant/storage-location master data and stock categories. For inspection-relevant material also check QM inspection setup at the plant.
Receiving must establish the actual stock segment and location.
A receiving address can still matter even when no unrestricted-use stock is created.
category: SPRO → Materials Management → Purchasing → [document] → Define Document Types. Check allowed item categories and their standard process controls.
Ordinarily expects a stock receipt and invoice.
The vendor retains ownership until withdrawal or transfer to own stock; settlement follows the consignment process.
assignment: SPRO → Materials Management → Purchasing → Account Assignment → Maintain Account Assignment Categories (OME9). Review account-assignment field selection and relevant cost-object master data.
An ordinary stock purchase generally uses a blank account assignment. Posting accounts are derived at the relevant goods movement.
A cost centre and applicable consumption account identify who bears the expense and which G/L is charged.
account gl costcenter asset distribution splitpercent
quantity: Check item and schedule-line data, procurement status and the unit conversion. A reference can be adopted only in part.
100 requested, 100 ordered: no residual request in this example.
100 requested, 80 ordered, 60 delivered: 20 outside this order and 20 open for delivery, subject to closing indicators.
units: Check the material’s additional units of measure, supplier-specific purchasing info and the conversion stored in the item.
60 pieces priced per piece need no physical-unit conversion.
Five cartons at 12 pieces per carton equals 60 pieces. At 240 per 100 pieces the simple goods value is 144.
schedule: Check plant MRP data, factory calendar, purchasing processing time, supplier-specific lead time and the saved document dates, as relevant.
A requester selects a required delivery date.
Scheduling works backward from required availability using the applicable lead times and calendars.
pr: Display the PR item and its status in ME53N. Inspect document type, field selection, origin, source and follow-on references before interpreting its worklist status.
The item can still be awaiting approval or assignment to a source.
Compare referenced order quantity and closing indicator; a worklist is a filtered view.
receipt: Review the item category and OME9 for account-assigned items. In ME23N inspect Item details → Delivery and Invoice. For PRs inspect Valuation and the account assignment.
Goods receipt is expected; a normal valuated stock receipt updates quantity and inventory value. GR non-valuated is not a general switch for stock purchasing.
The category and PO flags govern whether receipt is expected and valued. For a supported non-valuated receipt, cost recognition generally moves to invoice.
invoice: Inspect item category, account assignment controls in OME9 where relevant, invoice indicators and the actual invoice document. Consult Finance for tax and payment rules.
The expected supplier invoice, its posting and eventual payment are distinct events.
For supplier consignment, examine withdrawal and settlement instead of expecting an ordinary invoice against receipt.
grbased: Check the supplier’s purchasing data, the applicable purchasing info record and the saved PO’s Invoice tab. Inspect material-document references in invoice items.
The PO item supplies the matching context.
Two receipts against one item can be individually referenced in invoice verification.
source: Check source-list validity, quota arrangements, purchasing info records and contract validity for this material, plant and date. Inspect the source assigned to the actual item.
A preference on the PR can guide the buyer without establishing a firm source.
Check the fixed vendor or agreement item and its validity for the relevant requirement.
pricing: MM → Purchasing → Conditions → Define Price Determination Process. Inspect document condition analysis, valid condition records and manual entry where applicable. For a PR estimate inspect its valuation data.
The effective date, organization, unit and quantity scale select the relevant condition.
A reference or permitted manual entry may produce a different saved price. Reconstruct the actual subtotal.
net per bprme cond currency estimate
supplier: Inspect supplier general, purchasing organization and company-code data at the relevant levels, plus applicable partner functions.
Purchasing data can supply order-specific proposals.
The actual invoicing partner and its company-code data determine the financial context.
deliveryTerms: Inspect supplier purchasing data, agreement and actual item/header delivery terms. Verify the named place or address on supplier output.
The ordered plant often supplies the receiving address.
An alternate address or different named place can change supplier instructions and freight comparison.
tolerance: Inspect the tolerance values on the saved PO item and applicable purchasing-value-key or source defaults. Invoice tolerance limits are a separate configuration area.
98 of 100 may be accepted as complete under the applicable underdelivery tolerance and completion settings.
105 of 100 may meet a 5% overdelivery tolerance; inspect any unlimited flag before predicting the next receipt.
returns: Review the original receipt, movement reference and invoice status. Match the selected purchasing return route with Inventory Management.
Reverse or correct the erroneous document using the permitted reference.
Use the authorized return process and trace the vendor credit separately.
infoUpdate: Review purchasing default values for buyers, the document type and the current info record at purchasing-organization and plant level.
Take a before snapshot of conditions and the price history.
Compare the actual update scope for this document category and selected value.
contract: Purchasing → Contract → Define Document Types and Define Screen Layout at Document Level. Review agreement/item scope and release documentation in ME33K.
Example target 1,000 pieces; releases of 250 and 300 leave 450 against the target before adjustments.
Example target 10,000; releases of 3,000 and 4,500 leave 2,500 on the stated common valuation basis.
agr agreementitem targetqty targetval start end relorders
confirm: Purchasing → Confirmations. Inspect the confirmation-control key, confirmation sequence and data received from the supplier.
A requirement for an acknowledgement says the buyer expects a response.
An actual confirmation line has its own reference, date and quantity.
history: Inspect the individual item and its referenced purchasing history in display mode. Date, sign, unit and reference are all material to interpreting a balance.
An order can be saved without any receipt or invoice history.
80 received less a reversal of 10 leaves 70 net. An invoice for 80 is ten above that figure.
history gr ir delcomp final delete
rfq: Purchasing → RFQ and Quotation → document types and document-level screen layout. Inspect the invitation and the vendor’s recorded response.
Vendor-specific RFQ number, common requirement and quotation deadline.
ME47 records offered prices and terms against that invitation; each vendor response retains its identity.
compare: Run the classic price comparison with the desired RFQ selection, currency and price basis. Inspect the underlying quotation conditions when ranking is unexpected.
600 pieces at 8.50 plus 240 freight totals 5,340 before tax.
87 per ten, freight included, gives 5,220 on the same delivered basis.
texts: Purchasing → Texts for Purchasing Documents. Check relevant text types, copying rules and the output form where print behavior matters.
Compare text source and adoption settings for the item.
Read the actual issued output and distinguish a saved change from a reissued document.
service: Inspect classic External Services Management, document and item category, service specification, applicable limits and acceptance workflow.
Specific service lines, quantities and agreed rates supply the basis for acceptance.
The approved limit and actual entered/accepted services control the investigation.
approval: Classic release procedure with classification in Purchasing. Compare strategy characteristics, prerequisites, release codes and indicator/changeability settings.
Test document characteristics and their actual values at the evaluation time.
Inspect release status, required codes, prerequisites and authorizations.

fields.name: Document type
fields.purpose: Chooses the commercial document variant, including its number-range and field-selection context.
fields.origin: Create-screen default or an explicit selection. A copied document may propose a type.
fields.control: Choose an allowed type for this document category. A type used for a PO cannot simply turn it into an RFQ.
fields.effect: The type influences item categories, numbering and processing. Inspect the saved value when comparing standard and Z documents.
fields.trace: A PR and its follow-on PO each have their own type; a matching abbreviation does not establish the same configuration.
fields.qa: Create identical material items under a standard type and a client copy. Compare field selection and numbering separately.

fields.name: Material number
fields.purpose: Identifies the material to which the item refers and supplies a key to organization-specific master data.
fields.origin: Entered, searched from the catalog or copied from a referenced item. Relevant master data supplies proposals.
fields.control: An identified stock material and a permitted free-text consumable item use different minimum data. Item category and account assignment constrain the choice.
fields.effect: A valid number at client level may still lack required plant or valuation data.
fields.trace: Compare the material on PR, RFQ and saved PO. For a text item follow description, material group and references instead.
fields.qa: Compare a material item with a permissible text item in QA. Record which extra entries are requested.

fields.name: Short text
fields.purpose: Describes what the buyer or supplier should recognize on this item.
fields.origin: Usually proposed from material description when a number is supplied; entered by the user for free text or copied from a reference.
fields.control: A free-text item needs a meaningful description. Display mode locks it even when text was editable at creation.
fields.effect: It communicates scope. A changed description does not redefine the technical material identity.
fields.trace: Compare the text on the saved order and its predecessor; later master-data changes do not prove the text changed on an existing document.
fields.qa: Create a free-text item and compare its saved description with the request and supplier output.

fields.name: Material group
fields.purpose: Classifies spend or materials for buying and analysis. It is especially important when there is no material number.
fields.origin: Material master, referenced item or manual entry on a free-text line.
fields.control: A populated field can be required. Field-selection keys and item category determine the actual screen status; a master-data default may already satisfy it.
fields.effect: Buyers can group requirements and analyze purchasing by material group; additional client rules may also use it.
fields.trace: Compare the master-data group with the actual request and follow-on item. Check whether manual changes were permitted.
fields.qa: For an NB PO and standard item compare ME21N, AKTV, NBF and PT0F field selection for Material Group.
scenarios: In SAP’s documented combination PT0F makes Material Group required. A material master may fill it automatically.
Material master may supply no group. Enter the group when required by effective field selection and the item validations.

fields.name: Plant
fields.purpose: Identifies the site whose procurement or delivery requirement is being processed.
fields.origin: Can come from personal defaults, a reference or manual entry; material plant data helps validate the combination.
fields.control: Stock procurement needs a receiving plant. A centrally negotiated agreement can leave plant scope wider; the call-off must resolve it.
fields.effect: Plant affects sourcing, delivery address, available master data and valuation context.
fields.trace: Inspect the PR plant, agreement item restrictions and the plant on each actual PO item.
fields.qa: Use the same material in two plants. Check master-data extension and organization assignments before comparing prices.

fields.name: Storage location
fields.purpose: Identifies the storage location within the plant intended for the receipt.
fields.origin: Entered or proposed from a reference or the client’s procurement defaults.
fields.control: Frequently optional when ordering ordinary stock. A receipt into own stock normally needs the location at posting. Direct consumption follows a different route.
fields.effect: The posted material document determines where the stock actually went.
fields.trace: Follow the proposed location from request to order and compare it with the material document.
fields.qa: Prepare a PO with an empty location and a receipt with a valid location. Record where the value was first required.

fields.name: Item category
fields.purpose: Selects the procurement process for this line, such as standard goods, consignment, subcontracting or classic services.
fields.origin: User selection, document-type defaults or a permitted reference item.
fields.control: The document type limits permitted categories; item controls affect receipt, invoice and account assignment. A blank category displayed as Standard is meaningful.
fields.effect: The same material can follow a different inventory, ownership or service acceptance process.
fields.trace: Check the saved item category at each step and inspect the permitted conversions; code labels on screen can differ from stored internal values.
fields.qa: Compare standard and consignment items. Record which follow-on event makes the supplier payable in each case.

fields.name: Account assignment category
fields.purpose: States what kind of object receives the cost, for example K for cost centre or A for asset.
fields.origin: Entered on the requirement, proposed by the context, or copied into a follow-on document.
fields.control: Stock procurement can have a blank assignment. Consumption needs an appropriate category and its required account assignment details.
fields.effect: It determines the account assignment data and influences GR and IR settings. Asset and cost-centre cases have different accounting evidence.
fields.trace: Compare category, actual G/L and object on the PR, PO and accounting document; inspect the saved item before drawing a conclusion from current setup.
fields.qa: Create a stock line and a K line for the same material. Compare Account Assignment and Delivery sections.
scenarios: Blank account assignment; inventory account derived for a valuated receipt.
K determines cost-centre account assignment, expense destination and applicable GR/IR defaults.

fields.name: Cost centre
fields.purpose: Identifies the organizational cost object to which consumption is assigned.
fields.origin: Entered, defaulted by client rules or carried from a referenced account assignment.
fields.control: Relevant to a K item; a stock purchase normally has no cost-centre line. Validate the controlling area and period of validity.
fields.effect: The expense account describes the nature of cost; this object identifies the responsible centre.
fields.trace: Compare the account assignment distribution lines and actual cost assignment at GR or IR.
fields.qa: Split one item between two valid centres. Check the amounts on a supported partial posting.
scenarios: No K cost-centre assignment line in the ordinary stock case.
A valid cost centre is required for this example and must belong to the right controlling context.

fields.name: G/L account
fields.purpose: Identifies the expense or other applicable account on a purchasing account assignment.
fields.origin: Can be proposed by account determination or explicitly entered if the category and field controls allow.
fields.control: For a K line inspect OME9 and the actual G/L default. For ordinary stock, account determination supplies inventory postings during the movement.
fields.effect: Sets the expense-account destination for the account-assigned procurement case; verify the posted FI lines.
fields.trace: Trace the assignment from requisition to order. At posting check whether the expected account was taken from that assignment or determined for a stock transaction.
fields.qa: Compare a K line and a stock line of the same material. Identify the source of the account on each accounting document.
scenarios: FI account arises from the posting rules, including BSX where relevant.
The expense G/L belongs to the purchasing account assignment and may receive an automatic default.

fields.name: Asset number
fields.purpose: Identifies the capital asset in an asset-assigned purchase.
fields.origin: Selected from the asset master or copied with assignment data.
fields.control: Relevant for category A. Verify the correct company code and subnumber; observe the client’s acquisition and receipt-valuation design.
fields.effect: Links procurement to Asset Accounting. Acquisition timing can differ with the valuation treatment.
fields.trace: Follow asset and subnumber from the PO to the accounting and asset documents.
fields.qa: Compare the PO’s asset with its actual acquisition posting using a test asset and an approved QA scenario.

fields.name: Order as cost object
fields.purpose: Charges consumption to the order recorded in the account assignment.
fields.origin: Entered or inherited from the request that created the purchasing requirement.
fields.control: Depends on the account assignment category and a valid order that accepts the relevant postings.
fields.effect: The order can accumulate actual costs or commitments according to integration settings.
fields.trace: Follow the assigned order from requisition account detail to the actual posting. Keep it distinct from the purchasing document number.
fields.qa: Compare the same consumable bought for a cost centre and for an order. Identify the cost-object field that changes.

fields.name: WBS element
fields.purpose: Associates the procurement cost with a project work breakdown structure element.
fields.origin: Manual assignment or a project-related demand propagated to Purchasing.
fields.control: Depends on the project/account assignment scenario and object status. A project-consumption assignment and valuated project stock are different processes.
fields.effect: Controls the project context of commitments and actuals where active.
fields.trace: Compare the external WBS shown on-screen with the assignment in the subsequent document; F1 can show an internal identifier.
fields.qa: Trace the WBS on a QA project purchase through receipt and invoice and verify the object on the cost posting.

fields.name: Requested or ordered quantity
fields.purpose: States how many units the item calls for. Always read it together with its unit.
fields.origin: Entered, proposed by planning or adopted from the reference quantity, possibly only in part.
fields.control: A normal goods item needs a positive quantity. Limits and some service items use different value and quantity controls.
fields.effect: A partial reference or partial receipt leaves multiple open quantities at different stages.
fields.trace: Compare PR quantity, vendor quotation quantity, PO schedule lines and net receipt history in one unit.
fields.qa: Request 100, order 80 and receive 60. Calculate remaining demand and open delivery separately.

fields.name: Unit of measure
fields.purpose: Gives meaning to the item quantity. A box, a piece and a kilogram cannot be compared until a conversion is established.
fields.origin: Material base or order unit, supplier-specific data, reference document or explicit selection.
fields.control: Check whether the material permits the unit and whether a valid conversion to the base unit exists.
fields.effect: A unit mismatch can distort quantities and prices even when the numeric quantity appears correct.
fields.trace: Follow the registered unit and conversion on each document; the order-price unit can differ from the order unit.
fields.qa: Use five cartons of twelve pieces. Reconcile item quantity to sixty base pieces and compare the quoted price basis.

fields.name: Delivery date
fields.purpose: States the required or agreed delivery date for the item or schedule line.
fields.origin: Entered on a request, derived by scheduling, proposed from lead time or copied/adapted from a reference.
fields.control: An item can have multiple dated schedule lines. The PR field and the PO schedule table have different technical names.
fields.effect: Used for delivery monitoring and supply planning. It can differ from the date the material is available for use.
fields.trace: Compare the requested date with the ordered schedule date and any later vendor confirmation before judging lateness.
fields.qa: Split a 100-unit PO into dated quantities 60 and 40. Read each date independently of total quantity.
scenarios: 60 on 20 June and 40 on 27 June. Compare each promise with its own receipts.

fields.name: Requirement tracking number
fields.purpose: Adds a requester’s tracking reference shared by related purchasing items.
fields.origin: Entered manually or carried from the purchase requisition or reference item.
fields.control: Normally organizational, subject to the document’s field selection. It is separate from the system-generated PR number.
fields.effect: Supports finding related requirements; matching text alone is insufficient proof of a technical document link.
fields.trace: Compare copied references with the actual PR-item link in the PO.
fields.qa: Give two PR items the same tracking number and convert just one. Determine which item has a real PO reference.

fields.name: Goods receipt
fields.purpose: Tells Purchasing whether a receipt is expected for this item. A selected box describes the intended process; actual receipts appear in document history.
fields.origin: Item category and, for account-assigned items, the account assignment category’s receipt rules. Reference documents can supply proposed values.
fields.control: Ordinary standard stock procurement expects a GR. For K consumption inspect the authorized category settings in OME9 and the item. Display mode shows the saved choice.
fields.effect: Controls receipt relevance. The valuation of that receipt is governed separately, and GR-based invoice verification determines matching to specific deliveries.
fields.trace: Compare the item’s receipt indicator with MIGO eligibility and the later material document. A tick alone proves neither delivery nor an FI posting.
fields.qa: In QA compare a standard stock item with a K item. Predict quantity and value effects before posting a permitted receipt.
scenarios: Receipt expected. Check item-category controls before assuming the selected box is editable.
Receipt may be expected or optional according to OME9 and item controls; record the actual value and editability separately.

fields.name: GR non-valuated
fields.purpose: For applicable account-assigned purchases, specifies that the goods receipt is recorded without valuating that receipt.
fields.origin: The account assignment category can propose or constrain the value; check the actual saved item.
fields.control: Only applicable to supported item and account assignment combinations. It can be selected and non-editable due to process rules.
fields.effect: An applicable receipt records delivery without the normal value posting. Expense or acquisition recognition then follows the applicable invoice/asset process.
fields.trace: Compare the material or acceptance evidence at receipt with the FI documents at receipt and invoice. Do not infer this switch from the material type alone.
fields.qa: For a simple K purchase of 500, predict the expense posting for valuated and non-valuated GR. Compare the two accounting histories.
scenarios: Ordinary stock receipt carries valuation. This checkbox is generally inapplicable to the normal stock item.
Selected gives receipt evidence without the usual value posting at GR. The expense is recognized at invoice in the simple example.

fields.name: Invoice receipt
fields.purpose: States whether an invoice is expected against the purchasing item.
fields.origin: Usually proposed from item category and account assignment settings, with changes governed by those rules.
fields.control: Standard external purchases are typically invoice-relevant. A supplier consignment PO follows a settlement route with different invoice expectations.
fields.effect: Controls invoice relevance of the item. It records intention rather than confirming receipt of an invoice.
fields.trace: Read the saved indicator and inspect invoice documents or the correct settlement process separately.
fields.qa: Compare a standard stock PO with a supplier consignment item, then explain how the supplier obligation arises.
scenarios: Ordinary invoice receipt is not expected for the consignment item. Withdrawal and settlement establish the financial history.

fields.name: Requisitioner
fields.purpose: Names the person or requesting group who raised the requirement.
fields.origin: Manual entry, personal default or a generating process.
fields.control: Its input status depends on field selection. This field does not in itself authorize the request.
fields.effect: Gives the buyer a person or group to contact when scope is unclear.
fields.trace: Compare the requisitioner with creator and release authority; these can be three different people.
fields.qa: Open a requisition and locate evidence for requester, creator and approver separately.

fields.name: Desired vendor
fields.purpose: Records a supplier suggested by the requester.
fields.origin: Entered on the PR or populated by its origin.
fields.control: A preference is separate from firm source assignment. Check if the supplier is valid for the purchasing context.
fields.effect: Provides a suggestion for processing; it does not itself prove an order was issued to that supplier.
fields.trace: Compare the desired supplier, fixed vendor and actual PO supplier.
fields.qa: Enter a desired source on a test request and inspect what is actually assigned after sourcing.

fields.name: Fixed vendor
fields.purpose: Identifies the supplier assigned as the fixed source on the PR item.
fields.origin: Assigned by the buyer or applicable source determination.
fields.control: Requires a suitable source for the organizational and validity context. Compare against desired vendor.
fields.effect: Makes the sourcing decision visible for conversion; other conditions for automatic ordering may still apply.
fields.trace: Follow the fixed source to the resulting PO item and inspect its agreement or info-record reference.
fields.qa: Compare a merely desired vendor with an assigned fixed vendor on identical test demand.

fields.name: Valuation price
fields.purpose: Gives an estimated unit value for internal valuation of the requisition.
fields.origin: Material valuation, reference values or manual estimate depending on the item and settings.
fields.control: Read the price together with its price unit and currency. A populated estimate can be editable in one scenario and protected in another.
fields.effect: Supports approval or commitment valuation where configured. It does not guarantee the vendor’s PO price.
fields.trace: Compare the PR valuation price against the actual net price in the saved PO and explain any divergence.
fields.qa: Request 20 units at an estimate of 50; obtain a quote at 48 and distinguish the two document values.

fields.name: Price unit of estimate
fields.purpose: Number of units for which the requisition valuation price is quoted.
fields.origin: Proposed with the valuation price or entered for the estimate.
fields.control: Read jointly with price and unit; a value per 100 must not be interpreted as per piece.
fields.effect: Affects the estimated requisition value used by later decisions.
fields.trace: Convert the PR estimate to per-piece value before comparing with the vendor quotation.
fields.qa: Compare 600 per 100 with 6 per 1 for a requisition of 50.

fields.name: Requisition closed
fields.purpose: Indicates that further purchasing against this requested quantity is no longer expected.
fields.origin: Buyer or document processing according to the closing behavior of the requisition.
fields.control: Investigate order references and the reason for closure when a partly ordered request disappears from an open list.
fields.effect: Changes handling of outstanding requirements. Closed status alone cannot tell how many units were actually ordered or received.
fields.trace: Compare PR closed status with cumulative referenced order quantity and separate PO receipt history.
fields.qa: Order eight out of twelve requested units and compare the open requirement before and after authorized closure.

fields.name: Vendor
fields.purpose: Identifies the supplier for this purchasing document.
fields.origin: Entered by the buyer, selected by source determination or adopted from the referenced agreement or quotation.
fields.control: A stock purchase and a consumption purchase can share the same vendor. Ordering, invoicing and supplying partners may differ.
fields.effect: Sets the commercial partner and influences terms, currency and source-specific pricing.
fields.trace: Identify the vendor on the invitation, the quotation and the issued order; verify invoicing party separately.
fields.qa: Compare two suppliers for the same material and identify which header defaults change.

fields.name: Purchasing group
fields.purpose: Identifies the buyer or team responsible for procurement.
fields.origin: Item or plant material data, user defaults or explicit entry; compare the saved value.
fields.control: In PR processing the group is item-specific. In an external purchasing document it belongs to the header.
fields.effect: Supports workload assignment, selection and reporting. It does not alone define the legal buying entity.
fields.trace: Check how several PR items from different buyer groups were consolidated on an order.
fields.qa: Compare the same material in two plants and locate the buyer group on each request and order.

fields.name: Purchasing organization
fields.purpose: Identifies the purchasing unit responsible for the supplier relationship and negotiated conditions.
fields.origin: Organizational defaults, assigned source or a reference document.
fields.control: A request may initially have limited sourcing data; an external purchasing document needs its purchasing organization resolved.
fields.effect: Determines the purchasing context for vendor and agreement eligibility.
fields.trace: Check supplier data and conditions for the organization actually used, especially for cross-plant procurement.
fields.qa: Attempt to reference an agreement from another purchasing organization in QA; record whether the organizational design permits it.

fields.name: Company code
fields.purpose: Identifies the legal accounting entity for the purchasing document.
fields.origin: Organizational assignments, document context or explicit entry.
fields.control: Check compatibility between company code, plant and purchasing organization. A central agreement can have broader scope depending on design.
fields.effect: It defines the financial context for follow-on postings and the applicable company-code supplier data.
fields.trace: Compare the company code in the purchasing and accounting documents, including cross-company cases.
fields.qa: Compare one supplier’s purchasing data and company-code data and identify which set supports a payable.

fields.name: Document date
fields.purpose: Records the purchasing document date.
fields.origin: Often proposed from the current date or inherited through document creation; inspect the saved date.
fields.control: Document date, creation timestamp, delivery date and accounting posting date represent different events.
fields.effect: Supports document history and can matter to date-dependent commercial decisions under the configured rules.
fields.trace: Compare offer, order and delivery dates with the condition validity and pricing date actually used.
fields.qa: Display a historical order and distinguish document creation, physical delivery and posting dates.

fields.name: Currency
fields.purpose: Sets the currency for amounts in this purchasing document.
fields.origin: Supplier purchasing data, reference, or buyer entry depending on process.
fields.control: Compare currency with condition currency and company-code currency. The same numeral in two currencies has different value.
fields.effect: Affects comparisons and conversion to local-currency postings.
fields.trace: Trace a supplier’s foreign-currency price through the quotation, PO and local-currency documents.
fields.qa: Compare two quotes expressed in different currencies using a documented comparison date and rate.

fields.name: Payment terms
fields.purpose: Defines the agreed payment schedule and possible cash discount terms.
fields.origin: Often proposed from vendor purchasing data or a reference document; can be adjusted where allowed.
fields.control: Do not infer the due date from the bare key. The invoice baseline date and actual saved invoice terms matter.
fields.effect: Affects AP’s due-date and discount calculations according to invoice settings.
fields.trace: Compare terms on vendor, PO and posted invoice before diagnosing a missed discount.
fields.qa: Compare a 30-day term with a discounted term on two test invoices using the same baseline date.

fields.name: Incoterms
fields.purpose: Records the delivery term agreed with the supplier; the named place supplies essential context.
fields.origin: Supplier data, agreement, quotation or manual entry.
fields.control: Check the term and place together. Presence of a term does not by itself create a freight condition.
fields.effect: Communicates delivery responsibilities and helps interpret freight-inclusive comparisons.
fields.trace: Follow delivery terms from the supplier offer into the PO and check whether freight was also priced separately.
fields.qa: Compare two offers with different delivery terms at the same named destination.

fields.name: Incoterms location
fields.purpose: Qualifies the delivery term with a named place in classic ECC.
fields.origin: Proposed with the term or entered according to the agreement.
fields.control: Use the actual agreed place; two identical Incoterms codes at different locations can have different commercial implications.
fields.effect: Supports a meaningful handoff to receiving, shipping and invoice review.
fields.trace: Compare the named place in quotation or contract, saved PO and output.
fields.qa: Review two PO copies with the same Incoterms code but different locations. Decide which further freight evidence is needed.

fields.name: Net price
fields.purpose: States the item price for the specified price unit and order price unit.
fields.origin: Can be derived from conditions, an agreement, quotation, info record or manual price depending on scope.
fields.control: A calculated or locked item price can still have underlying editable condition lines. Check pricing and price-display permissions.
fields.effect: Affects commercial value and the reference used by invoice verification.
fields.trace: Trace the selected offer or agreement, the PO conditions and invoice comparison on the same unit basis.
fields.qa: Compare 12 per one and 1,200 per hundred. Confirm whether the PO derives the same goods value.

fields.name: Price unit
fields.purpose: Numeric denominator for the quoted item price, such as 1 or 100.
fields.origin: Adopted with conditions or entered with the price.
fields.control: Always pair with the order price unit. Price per hundred pieces differs from price per hundred cartons.
fields.effect: An incorrect denominator scales the item value and invoice expectation.
fields.trace: Trace the denominator in offer, agreement and PO rather than comparing only net price.
fields.qa: Quote 240 per 100 pieces and order 60 pieces. Check the resulting 144 before additional conditions.

fields.name: Order price unit
fields.purpose: Specifies the physical unit in which the vendor quotes the price.
fields.origin: Purchasing info record, conditions, reference document or explicit entry.
fields.control: May differ from the order unit. The item needs a consistent conversion between the two.
fields.effect: Changes the price quantity used in order and invoice comparison.
fields.trace: Read the unit relationship on the saved order and the actual price quantity used during invoicing.
fields.qa: Order cartons but price per piece. Verify both the unit conversion and numerical price unit.

fields.name: Condition type and amount
fields.purpose: Identifies a pricing component such as base price, discount or freight.
fields.origin: Condition access can find a record valid for the date and key; commercial terms may also be entered manually.
fields.control: The schema, access sequence, validity and manual-entry settings govern individual conditions. Statistical lines may be displayed separately.
fields.effect: Conditions build the item price and effective comparison components. Use the pricing basis and subtotals to explain the arithmetic.
fields.trace: Compare the saved condition analysis with the source record valid at creation time.
fields.qa: Rebuild a line with a base of 1,200, discount of 120 and freight of 60; identify the subtotal being compared.

fields.name: GR-based invoice verification
fields.purpose: Matches the invoice to individual goods receipts for the PO item.
fields.origin: Supplier purchasing data, applicable info record or purchase reference may propose it. Examine the actual item.
fields.control: The receipt must be relevant to the process. Check field selection, prerequisites and existing history before changing a saved PO.
fields.effect: Partial deliveries remain distinguishable for invoice matching. Selecting Goods Receipt alone does not establish GR-based IV.
fields.trace: Trace a delivery’s material document into invoice item references rather than matching only a PO total.
fields.qa: Receive 6 units and then 4. Open invoice entry for the PO and inspect how the deliveries are proposed.

fields.name: Delivery completed
fields.purpose: Signals that further deliveries are no longer expected for this PO item.
fields.origin: Can be set by the user or by receiving logic, including client tolerance settings.
fields.control: It can be set on a short but accepted final delivery. It is a completion indicator; do not assume it prohibits every later posting.
fields.effect: Affects open-delivery quantity and monitoring. The actual received quantity still comes from history.
fields.trace: Compare the completion indicator and receipt history, including reversals.
fields.qa: Order 100, accept a last delivery totalling 98 within an agreed tolerance, and compare history with the open quantity report.

fields.name: Underdelivery tolerance
fields.purpose: Percentage shortfall acceptable relative to the ordered quantity for delivery completion.
fields.origin: Purchasing value key, source data, reference or item-specific entry depending on settings.
fields.control: The relevant percentage works with completion logic; a partial receipt is not automatically a business decision to close the PO.
fields.effect: Can affect whether a short final delivery qualifies for completion.
fields.trace: Compare ordered, received and still-expected quantities on the actual item.
fields.qa: Test 97, 98 and 99 against 100 ordered with a 2 percent underdelivery tolerance; record completion behavior.

fields.name: Overdelivery tolerance
fields.purpose: Percentage by which delivery can exceed ordered quantity under the item’s tolerance.
fields.origin: May be proposed from purchasing data or copied and adjusted.
fields.control: Check Unlimited overdelivery and actual message behavior before predicting acceptance.
fields.effect: Controls overdelivery checks at receiving; it is separate from invoice variance limits.
fields.trace: Compare cumulative net receipts with order quantity and this tolerance.
fields.qa: For 100 ordered with a 5 percent tolerance and unlimited off, compare proposed receipts totalling 105 and 106.

fields.name: Unlimited overdelivery
fields.purpose: Permits delivery beyond the ordinary item percentage ceiling under the overdelivery check.
fields.origin: Item proposal or user setting where enabled.
fields.control: An unchecked indicator leaves the percentage limit relevant. Other validity, quantity and stock checks still apply.
fields.effect: Affects goods-receipt quantity checks without defining the invoice acceptance decision.
fields.trace: Read the indicator on the effective PO item, then separately review invoiced-versus-received history.
fields.qa: Repeat the same excess quantity in QA with the flag off and on, keeping every other input fixed.

fields.name: Final invoice
fields.purpose: Signals that no further invoice is expected for this purchasing item.
fields.origin: Set by invoice processing or on the PO as appropriate to the case.
fields.control: It does not establish that the vendor has been paid or that no future invoice can technically be entered.
fields.effect: Can affect outstanding commitment handling. GR/IR and the vendor account still require their own evidence.
fields.trace: Compare the final-invoice flag, open commitments, invoice history and payment clearing separately.
fields.qa: Find a PO item marked final invoice and determine what evidence proves actual vendor payment.

fields.name: Tax code
fields.purpose: Identifies the input-tax treatment expected for the purchase in the client’s tax procedure.
fields.origin: May be proposed by purchasing data or determined/entered according to local configuration.
fields.control: Confirm the actual code with Finance for the company and transaction. A blank or zero-rate code has meaning only in its tax context.
fields.effect: Used in tax calculation and checking; deductions and postings depend on the configured tax treatment.
fields.trace: Compare PO tax information with the supplier invoice and FI tax lines.
fields.qa: In QA compare the same net value with two Finance-approved sample codes and inspect the tax basis.

fields.name: Returns item
fields.purpose: Marks the purchasing item as a returns-to-vendor process.
fields.origin: Selected for the returns PO item or copied from a suitable reference.
fields.control: It represents a commercial return, distinct from correcting an erroneously posted goods receipt.
fields.effect: Changes the expected direction of logistics and invoice/credit processing.
fields.trace: Trace the returns item to the actual goods movement and supplier credit; neither alone proves the other happened.
fields.qa: Compare a physical return of four goods with correction of an accidentally overstated receipt by four.

fields.name: Purchasing info record
fields.purpose: Identifies supplier/material purchasing information relevant to the item.
fields.origin: Proposed through source determination or selected by the buyer.
fields.control: Read the purchasing organization, plant scope, category and validity. Multiple sources of conditions can apply.
fields.effect: Supports order-unit, delivery and price proposals according to the actual source configuration.
fields.trace: Compare current info-record values with the condition analysis on a saved PO.
fields.qa: Check two orders on opposite sides of a condition-validity date and establish their actual price sources.

fields.name: Info update
fields.purpose: Controls whether purchasing information is updated by this document in the supported update context.
fields.origin: Purchasing default values or explicit selection; behavior depends on document type, release and existing info records.
fields.control: Review the exact indicator presentation in the transaction. A check mark does not guarantee every existing master condition is replaced.
fields.effect: Can influence purchasing info records or order-price history used in later buying.
fields.trace: Record the existing info-record data before saving the test document and compare the affected organizational level afterward.
fields.qa: Create two test documents differing only in Info update; compare resulting source data without assuming all fields update.

fields.name: Agreement reference
fields.purpose: Identifies the outline agreement selected as the source of this item.
fields.origin: Sourcing, reference adoption or manual agreement assignment.
fields.control: Check vendor, organization, item and validity. Typing the supplier and price without a reference does not create a release against the contract.
fields.effect: Makes downstream release documentation and agreement consumption traceable.
fields.trace: Follow the PR source to the PO’s agreement number and item, then inspect contract release documentation.
fields.qa: Compare a referenced call-off with a standalone PO to the same supplier at the same price.

fields.name: Purchase requisition reference
fields.purpose: Records the requisition from which the buyer adopted this PO item.
fields.origin: Set when the order item actually references the PR item.
fields.control: Read the requisition number and item together. Similar text or tracking numbers do not prove a reference.
fields.effect: Supports PR processing status and tracing ordered versus requested quantities.
fields.trace: Use the PO item’s requisition reference and compare the corresponding ordered quantity in the PR.
fields.qa: Compare a manually typed copy with an item adopted from the PR document overview.

fields.name: Confirmation control key
fields.purpose: Defines which supplier confirmations are expected and how they are processed.
fields.origin: May be proposed from the supplier or purchasing info record, depending on the setup.
fields.control: Check the configured confirmation sequence and the item. A requested date and a vendor-confirmed date are separate data.
fields.effect: Can influence monitoring and planning relevance of expected confirmations and inbound deliveries.
fields.trace: Compare the order schedule line, recorded acknowledgement and confirmed schedule quantities.
fields.qa: Record a sample order acknowledgement with a changed delivery date; identify each date separately.

fields.name: Acknowledgment required
fields.purpose: Requests a supplier order acknowledgement for the item.
fields.origin: Purchasing proposals, source data or item entry.
fields.control: A selected requirement does not itself record that an acknowledgement arrived.
fields.effect: Supports supplier follow-up and reminder handling in the configured process.
fields.trace: Trace requirement, actual confirmation and evidence of output to the vendor independently.
fields.qa: Review an item requiring acknowledgment and show what evidence would establish the supplier actually replied.

fields.name: Planned delivery time
fields.purpose: Number of calendar days used for the supplier delivery interval in relevant scheduling.
fields.origin: Often proposed from applicable purchasing or material master data.
fields.control: Read alongside purchasing and GR processing times and their calendars. A planned interval is not a supplier confirmation.
fields.effect: Can influence dates and planning assumptions. It does not prove when the shipment will arrive.
fields.trace: Compare the master proposal, saved item and actual confirmed date.
fields.qa: Hold demand constant and vary the planned lead time on a QA planning example.

fields.name: GR processing time
fields.purpose: Time for internal receiving activities before material is available to use.
fields.origin: Usually supplied by material/plant planning data, subject to the procurement context.
fields.control: Distinguish working days for processing from the supplier’s planned delivery interval.
fields.effect: Helps explain why a required availability date can be later than receipt at the dock.
fields.trace: Work backwards from requirement date to receipt and procurement dates using the actual calendars.
fields.qa: Allow two receiving workdays and test a receipt just before a weekend.

fields.name: Purchase order history
fields.purpose: Shows follow-on events referring to the selected order item.
fields.origin: Generated from posted receipts, reversals, invoices or other relevant follow-on documents.
fields.control: Display-only evidence. The History tab can be absent or empty before relevant postings exist.
fields.effect: Helps reconcile the ordered, delivered and invoiced quantities and values at item level.
fields.trace: Open individual material and invoice documents; apply the correct sign to reversals and use consistent units.
fields.qa: Receive 80, reverse 10, invoice 80 and explain the 10-piece discrepancy without using a header total.

fields.name: Collective RFQ number
fields.purpose: Groups separate vendor invitations belonging to the same sourcing event.
fields.origin: Typically entered by the buyer and reused on the participating RFQs; on the comparison screen it can be used for selection.
fields.control: A vendor-specific RFQ number remains distinct. Matching collective numbers do not guarantee identical items or conditions.
fields.effect: Helps retrieve all responses for the bid comparison.
fields.trace: Follow the collective number to each RFQ and quotation, then compare the actual material items and quantities.
fields.qa: Give two invitations the same collective number, enter one response and inspect the comparison selection.

fields.name: Quotation deadline
fields.purpose: Last requested date for the supplier’s offer.
fields.origin: Buyer enters it with the invitation or copies it from the RFQ being reused.
fields.control: It differs from the required delivery date and from the validity of the supplier’s quotation.
fields.effect: Defines the response timetable for purchasing follow-up.
fields.trace: Compare invited deadline, vendor response date and date the offer expires before evaluating timeliness.
fields.qa: Use the same response deadline with two different item delivery dates and explain which date the supplier must meet for each event.

fields.name: Invited vendor
fields.purpose: Identifies the vendor addressed by this RFQ.
fields.origin: Selected when addressing the RFQ; multiple suppliers in a sourcing event generally have individually identifiable RFQs.
fields.control: Vendor master data and organizational context must support the invitation. A collective number can join invitations.
fields.effect: Provides the recipient and the reference under which its quotation is maintained.
fields.trace: Compare the vendor-specific invitation number with the ME47 quotation and collective comparison list.
fields.qa: Prepare two invitations for identical items; explain how the responses stay attributable to each vendor.

fields.name: Supplier quotation number
fields.purpose: Records the supplier’s own offer reference.
fields.origin: Entered from the supplier’s response during quotation maintenance.
fields.control: Distinguish the vendor’s reference from the internal RFQ number and the collective RFQ number.
fields.effect: Helps identify the commercial evidence used in the award.
fields.trace: Compare the supplier PDF or letter with the saved offer reference and any reference carried forward.
fields.qa: Identify all three identifiers for a sample event and describe when each should be used.

fields.name: Rejection indicator
fields.purpose: Records the buyer’s rejection of the quotation item in the classic RFQ process.
fields.origin: Buyer’s evaluation decision after reviewing the offer.
fields.control: It is an item decision. Actual rejection communication depends on message/output processing.
fields.effect: Supports rejection follow-up and documenting which offer was declined.
fields.trace: Trace the offered item, comparison basis, saved rejection and any output separately.
fields.qa: Reject one line of a two-item test quotation and inspect which item and output are affected.
scenarios: Buyer may record the rejection after evaluation.
Decision is displayed; a rejection record and outgoing rejection communication are separate evidence.

fields.name: RFQ selection
fields.purpose: Identifies the invitations whose vendor responses will be compared.
fields.origin: Entered directly or selected using organizational or collective RFQ criteria.
fields.control: This is a reporting selection. The source RFQ and quotation records remain separate documents in the purchasing process.
fields.effect: Determines which offers enter the list; a missing offer can arise from selection or missing quotation data.
fields.trace: Trace each displayed comparison column back to its vendor-specific RFQ item.
fields.qa: Compare a search by RFQ number with the collective-number selection for the same event.

fields.name: Comparison currency
fields.purpose: Expresses prices from different offers on a common currency basis.
fields.origin: Entered or proposed for the comparison run.
fields.control: Review exchange rate basis and conversion date. A ranking in another currency can depend on exchange rates and rounding.
fields.effect: Changes the presentation and calculated comparisons, without changing the saved supplier quotations.
fields.trace: Recalculate one converted price from the supplier’s currency and documented rate.
fields.qa: Run the same two foreign-currency offers in a common currency and reconstruct one item manually.

fields.name: Comparison price and scope
fields.purpose: Controls the price basis and optional components in a quotation comparison.
fields.origin: Selected for the comparison run according to the report’s available choices.
fields.control: Read which freight, delivery costs, discounts and other components are included. Time-dependent conditions and setup may limit comparison.
fields.effect: Influences the apparent cheapest offer. Delivery or quality trade-offs still require evaluation.
fields.trace: Rebuild the effective comparison value from the recorded quotation components.
fields.qa: Compare a low base price plus freight with a higher delivered price. Document the assumptions that reverse the ranking.

fields.name: Rank and relative price
fields.purpose: Shows a supplier’s relative position on the selected comparison basis.
fields.origin: Calculated by the report from the included offers and selection options.
fields.control: Display-only result. A missing price and a zero-price offer are different cases.
fields.effect: Supports evaluation but does not create an award, contract or PO.
fields.trace: Trace a surprising ranking to the actual quotation item, price unit, currency, validity and comparison selections.
fields.qa: Explain a ranking for 600 pieces priced per carton by one vendor and per piece by another.

fields.name: Validity begins
fields.purpose: Starts the period in which the purchasing agreement is intended to apply.
fields.origin: Entered from negotiated terms.
fields.control: Compare the header interval with item condition validity. The commercial conditions can change within one agreement period.
fields.effect: Affects source selection and whether a call-off is within the agreed window.
fields.trace: Compare agreement validity, condition date and call-off document date.
fields.qa: Try one QA release order inside the interval and another outside; record the actual message and rule.

fields.name: Validity ends
fields.purpose: Last date of the contract’s validity period.
fields.origin: Entered from the agreement or an approved extension.
fields.control: Inspect the actual date on the agreement and the relevant comparison or release-order date. Client message settings can influence processing.
fields.effect: Supports expiry follow-up and checks when referencing the agreement.
fields.trace: Distinguish an expired agreement from an agreement with valid header dates but expired price conditions.
fields.qa: Hold the item constant and vary only the date around the end of the interval.

fields.name: Target quantity
fields.purpose: Agreed target quantity for a quantity-contract item.
fields.origin: Entered from the negotiated volume and unit.
fields.control: Central to a quantity contract. A value contract is assessed chiefly by its target value.
fields.effect: Provides a basis for monitoring release-order quantities; goods receipt has separate status.
fields.trace: Compare 1,000 target units, 550 called off and 400 received. Agreement consumption and delivered quantity differ.
fields.qa: Create two referenced call-offs for 250 and 300 and review release documentation.
scenarios: The agreed quantity is the primary target.
Evaluate the monetary agreement target and release values.

fields.name: Target value
fields.purpose: Monetary target of the value contract in its document currency.
fields.origin: Entered from the negotiated value ceiling.
fields.control: Especially relevant to value contracts. Never compare a target in one currency with a raw release total in another.
fields.effect: Supports monitoring value consumed against the agreement. Exceedance message behavior is client-dependent.
fields.trace: Compare referenced order values and subsequent order changes against the reported releases.
fields.qa: For a target of 10,000, inspect releases of 3,000 and 4,500 in the same currency and calculate the provisional remaining value.
scenarios: Use target value with document currency and actual release values.
Quantity is the negotiated target. A monetary report answers a different question.

fields.name: Release documentation
fields.purpose: Shows call-offs created with reference to the contract or contract item.
fields.origin: Generated from referencing purchase orders and relevant changes.
fields.control: Read-only result; a separately created PO to the same vendor at the same price does not establish a release reference.
fields.effect: Shows agreement utilization, which differs from the physical quantity received.
fields.trace: Follow the release documentation into the actual PO item and then its receipt history.
fields.qa: Compare two otherwise identical POs, only one of which references the agreement.

fields.name: Condition validity period
fields.purpose: Marks the interval for which a time-dependent commercial condition applies.
fields.origin: Maintained with the condition record or negotiated terms where time-dependent conditions are used.
fields.control: Check document type and condition technique. Not all RFQ types use time-dependent conditions.
fields.effect: The same agreement can propose different prices for different pricing dates.
fields.trace: Trace the date on the PO pricing analysis to the matching validity interval.
fields.qa: Set up two non-overlapping test price periods and compare the resulting call-off prices.

fields.name: Delivery address
fields.purpose: Specifies the destination for this item, including an alternate address when appropriate.
fields.origin: Often derived from the receiving plant or storage location, or entered as an alternative delivery address.
fields.control: Some processes, including third-party purchasing, determine the destination differently. Inspect the actual item.
fields.effect: Controls delivery instructions communicated to the supplier and can differ from the accounting company address.
fields.trace: Compare customer, plant and manually maintained addresses with the issued PO output.
fields.qa: In a test order compare a plant delivery and an alternate address. Confirm which destination appears on the supplier document.

fields.name: Partner function
fields.purpose: Distinguishes business roles such as ordering address, goods supplier or invoicing party.
fields.origin: Vendor partner data and the document’s partner schema can propose business partners.
fields.control: Only permitted partner roles appear; mandatory roles and allowed changes depend on the selected procedure.
fields.effect: A supplier name on the PO does not guarantee every subsequent communication or invoice uses the same partner.
fields.trace: Compare the vendor, partner role, actual output recipient and invoicing party.
fields.qa: Inspect an order with a separate invoicing party and show which partner is used for which purpose.

fields.name: Item long text
fields.purpose: Adds item-specific instructions that exceed the short description.
fields.origin: Copied or proposed according to text determination, from material or purchasing master data, a reference or user entry.
fields.control: Different text types have different adoption and printing rules. Visibility in SAP does not promise printing.
fields.effect: Can communicate technical specifications or delivery instructions through the applicable output.
fields.trace: Compare the saved text ID and supplier output; header text and item text can follow different rules.
fields.qa: Add distinctive QA text to a print-relevant and internal text type; review a test output.

fields.name: Header long text
fields.purpose: Carries terms or instructions common to the order.
fields.origin: Text types and copying rules, master or predecessor document, or manual entry.
fields.control: The text displayed on-screen and the text selected by the form depend on configuration and output design.
fields.effect: Provides supplier-facing or internal information according to the chosen text type.
fields.trace: Trace changed text on the saved PO to a newly generated test output version.
fields.qa: Change a header text in a QA copy and identify whether all items share the statement and whether it prints.

fields.name: Supplier acknowledgement reference
fields.purpose: Records an external acknowledgement or confirmation identifier where used.
fields.origin: Entered from the supplier response or populated by an inbound interface.
fields.control: Read the confirmation category and relevant reference. A buyer’s tick requesting confirmation is a different field.
fields.effect: Allows the business to identify an actual acknowledgement against the order.
fields.trace: Match the response reference and date to the PO item and confirmation line.
fields.qa: Identify the evidence of an actual supplier response for a partial confirmation.

fields.name: Schedule line quantity
fields.purpose: Portion of the ordered quantity assigned to a particular date.
fields.origin: Proposed from the item quantity and maintained on one or more lines.
fields.control: Quantities across lines need to be consistent with the item total; received or confirmed history can restrict later changes.
fields.effect: Used for delivery scheduling and open requirements by date.
fields.trace: Compare the item total with individual schedule quantities, supplier confirmations and net receipts.
fields.qa: Split 100 into 60 this month and 40 next month, then show what the buyer should chase after receiving 60.
scenarios: 100 units on the single confirmed or required date.
60 and 40 on separate dates still total 100. Track each open line.

fields.name: Pricing date control
fields.purpose: Determines which relevant date is used to find conditions in the applicable pricing scenario.
fields.origin: Pricing-date rules and supplier or info-record proposals where used.
fields.control: A PO document date and chosen pricing date need not be identical. Review item behavior before forcing a new price.
fields.effect: Changes the validity record used when determining a price. A revised setup does not retroactively explain an old saved price.
fields.trace: Use the condition analysis and actual dates to reproduce the price rather than querying only current conditions.
fields.qa: Use two validity periods and compare a fresh determination on each side of the boundary.

fields.name: Account assignment distribution
fields.purpose: Defines how multiple assignment lines share a purchasing item.
fields.origin: Set with the item’s multiple account assignments.
fields.control: Use supported quantity, percentage or value options as offered by the document and release. Partial postings have additional distribution rules.
fields.effect: A balancing item total can still allocate an incorrect amount to each cost object.
fields.trace: Compare saved distribution lines with the actual split in a partial receipt or invoice.
fields.qa: Split 1,000 at 60/40, post a supported partial 500 and compare proportional versus sequential distribution if available.

fields.name: Requisition date
fields.purpose: Records the date of the internal request.
fields.origin: Proposed on creation or supplied by the originating process.
fields.control: Different from the required delivery date and the date at which a release decision is needed.
fields.effect: Useful for tracking elapsed processing time and identifying the age of demand.
fields.trace: Compare PR date, approval timestamp and date of the first referenced order.
fields.qa: Read a historical PR and distinguish age of demand from days until delivery.

fields.name: Release date for procurement
fields.purpose: Scheduling date by which procurement processing should start for the requirement.
fields.origin: Scheduling can calculate this from requirement timing and procurement lead times.
fields.control: Distinguish this planning date from the timestamp at which a person approved the requisition.
fields.effect: Supports scheduling and worklist timing; it is not proof that the PR passed release strategy.
fields.trace: Compare planned release date with actual approval history and PO creation date.
fields.qa: In a planned PR record all three dates and explain why they can differ.

fields.name: Valuation currency
fields.purpose: Currency for the estimated requisition value.
fields.origin: Derived or proposed from the relevant organizational context and valuation data.
fields.control: It belongs to the planning estimate. A supplier may later quote in a different currency.
fields.effect: Affects how a buyer compares the estimate with quotations and approval thresholds.
fields.trace: Carry the currency and price denominator when comparing estimated and ordered values.
fields.qa: Use one local-currency estimate and a foreign-currency quote. Document the rate used in your comparison.

fields.name: Stock type at receipt
fields.purpose: Indicates the planned stock category for the receipt, for example whether material is intended for inspection.
fields.origin: Item, material quality settings and receiving process can influence the proposal.
fields.control: QM integration and active inspection settings can determine the effective posting. Check both indicators and actual receipt.
fields.effect: Physical inventory can increase while unrestricted-use quantity remains unchanged.
fields.trace: Trace the purchase item to the actual material-document stock category and any inspection lot or stock transfer.
fields.qa: Receive a test inspection-relevant item and identify why production cannot immediately withdraw the whole quantity.

fields.name: Distribution percentage
fields.purpose: Share of item cost associated with one assignment line under percentage distribution.
fields.origin: Entered on each account assignment or copied from a referenced item.
fields.control: Only relevant to the applicable distribution mode. Check that the complete set reconciles to 100 percent.
fields.effect: Directs how value is apportioned across cost objects under the appropriate partial-posting rules.
fields.trace: Read the percentages together with the distribution rule and the posted account assignments.
fields.qa: Use 60 and 40 percent on two centres and verify a 500 partial receipt against the actual partial-distribution setting.

fields.name: Service specification
fields.purpose: Defines planned services, quantities, units and rates on a classic service PO.
fields.origin: Entered, adopted from PR/service specifications, or drawn from allowed master and contract data.
fields.control: Available for applicable classic service items. Planned service lines and unplanned service limits have different controls.
fields.effect: Forms the basis for entry and acceptance of services and later invoice checking.
fields.trace: Follow the ordered service line into the entry sheet and accepted quantity.
fields.qa: Order 80 hours, record 50 hours of work and compare the actually accepted amount with the original order.

fields.name: Overall limit and expected value
fields.purpose: Sets a value ceiling and a planning expectation for the applicable unplanned-service or limit process.
fields.origin: Buyer or requester enters values according to the required service scope and client approval policy.
fields.control: Relevant for the supported item category and release. Distinguish the absolute overall limit from expected value.
fields.effect: Allows control over actual unplanned work and estimated order value; acceptance and invoicing still require their own evidence.
fields.trace: Compare the saved limits with actual entries, business approval and invoice amount.
fields.qa: Set different overall and expected values and compare the order value with the allowed entry scenario.

fields.name: Release status and strategy
fields.purpose: Shows approval information for a purchasing document under classic release procedure.
fields.origin: Determined from configured strategy, characteristics and release actions when the procedure applies.
fields.control: Status information is read-only in the ordinary document view. Performing a release uses the appropriate action and authorization.
fields.effect: Can control further processing, issue or conversion according to the release indicator.
fields.trace: Trace classification values, the actual strategy found and which codes have acted. A delivery date is not an approval timestamp.
fields.qa: Compare two documents immediately below and above a client-approved test boundary and identify which characteristic selected the strategy.
scenarios: Approval status may be unset or proposed until the document is saved.
Read the selected strategy and completed release codes; approvals require the appropriate release function.

fields.name: Exchange rate
fields.purpose: Sets the document exchange-rate basis for foreign-currency purchasing.
fields.origin: Typically proposed from exchange-rate data for relevant currencies and date, or manually entered where allowed.
fields.control: Inspect the fixed-rate flag and actual follow-on posting rules before expecting the PO rate to appear in FI.
fields.effect: Influences conversion. A differing local amount may reflect date or rate treatment as well as unit price.
fields.trace: Compare the PO currency and rate to the exchange rate used on receipt and invoice.
fields.qa: Compare two otherwise identical foreign-currency orders on different dates; use simulated postings to identify effective rates.

fields.name: Exchange rate fixed
fields.purpose: Records whether a fixed exchange rate applies for this purchase order under the corresponding processing rules.
fields.origin: Buyer selection or document proposal where permitted.
fields.control: Depends on currency and client process. A tick without the actual saved rate is insufficient evidence.
fields.effect: Changes how relevant follow-on documents handle the order’s exchange rate.
fields.trace: Record PO rate, flag and actual posting dates before comparing GR and IR values.
fields.qa: Compare fixed and unfixed foreign-currency orders on a later posting date with a different maintained rate.
scenarios: Inspect the agreed saved rate and applicable follow-on rule.
A later posting date can use a different exchange rate. Compare actual FI evidence.

fields.name: Fixed requisition
fields.purpose: Identifies a firmed requisition in the planning context.
fields.origin: Can result from manual processing or firming logic depending on how the PR was created.
fields.control: A firmed item and an approved item describe different decisions. Check the creation origin and planning settings.
fields.effect: Can affect whether subsequent planning changes an existing proposal.
fields.trace: Compare MRP-generated proposals before and after firming, then inspect approval independently.
fields.qa: Change a test requirement and rerun planning with controlled parameters to compare firmed and unfirmed proposals.

fields.name: Contract item category for broad scope
fields.purpose: Identifies a contract scope such as material unknown or material group where the category is permitted.
fields.origin: Chosen when the agreement intentionally covers more than one specifically coded material.
fields.control: For classic M and W categories inspect which fields are required at agreement stage and which must be specified at release. Applicability differs by contract type.
fields.effect: Allows a broad agreement to be made specific when a release order is entered.
fields.trace: Compare material, material group, quantity, unit and price requirements on the original contract with the release item.
fields.qa: Compare a designated material item with a permitted material-group contract item and record where exact material and price become known.

fields.name: Agreement item number
fields.purpose: Identifies the precise outline agreement line used as a purchasing source.
fields.origin: Adopted with an agreement reference.
fields.control: The agreement number alone is insufficient when there are many conditions or different contracted items.
fields.effect: Assigns the call-off to the correct release documentation and commercial terms.
fields.trace: Trace the PO to the specific contract item and its conditions, then to the release quantities.
fields.qa: Test two eligible items under one agreement and verify which release total changes.

fields.name: Deletion indicator
fields.purpose: Marks the purchasing line for deletion within the supported document process.
fields.origin: Set by an authorized user or document process, subject to the state of the item.
fields.control: Restrictions depend on document processing and follow-on history. An indicator does not erase posted receipts or invoices.
fields.effect: Affects future use and worklists. Historical documents still need to be reconciled independently.
fields.trace: Compare deletion, delivery completion, final invoice and historical quantities independently.
